svg.title: From one Pod to one observed workload <size:14>Direct reader mode | Illustrative acquisition</size>

g.text: From one Pod to one observed workload
Direct reader mode. Illustrative objects and counts; no live cluster execution.
Consumer process (owns client, mapper and lifecycle)
The caller wraps its dynamic client and RESTMapper with clientgo.NewReader.
Construction performs no Kubernetes reads and starts no background work.
B. Find the starting object's workload
Exact GVK mappings determine resource and namespace scope.
Each edge checks identity, UID and scope; cycles, multiple controllers
and excessive depth fail. Mapping calls are abbreviated here.
Scope comes from the terminal root. A cluster-scoped root requires all namespaces.
Completed, terminating and unscheduled Pods remain in the list.
[Every listed Pod, including Pods outside this workload]
[Each required owner absent from this acquisition]
[Incomplete list, unreadable owner or invalid ownership]
Acquisition fails; no partial or false-empty workload is returned.
A changed or missing starting object during collection also fails.
[Exact root GVK has a Karta definition (this JobSet)]
observed.Root() is the terminal root; observed.Pods() retains all confirmed members.
Known kind: Definition() != nil, Generic() == false. Unknown kind: nil, true.
This is a detached observation, not a cross-resource Kubernetes transaction.
[A Pod may belong but attribution is unresolved]
A generic workload exposes its confirmed members through Component("pods").
These queries perform no reader or API calls. Unknown component or instance,
or a missing replica axis, returns an error. Outer scope bindings stay intact.
Acquire again to refresh. Local karta.Workload edits do not change this observation.
